title: Syntagma Square and the changing of the guard

name.label: supported
name.says: Syntagma means Constitution; it is named for the constitution King Otto had to grant after an uprising on 3 September 1843.
quote: "Constitution Square"
The square is named after the Constitution that Otto, the first King of Greece, was obliged to grant after a popular and military uprising on 3 September 1843.

capital.label: supported
capital.says: King Otto moved the capital from Nafplio to Athens in 1834.
quote: King Otto moved the capital of the newly born Greek Kingdom from Nafplio to Athens in 1834

palace-built.label: supported
palace-built.says: Building of the Old Royal Palace began in 1836.
quote: It was constructed between 1836

parliament.label: supported
parliament.says: In November 1929 the government decided the palace would house Parliament; the Senate first met there on 2 August 1934.
quote: until November 1929, when government decided that the building would permanently house Parliament
the Senate convened in the "Old Palace" (Παλαιά Ανάκτορα) on 2 August 1934

gartner.label: supported
gartner.says: The palace was designed by the Bavarian architect Friedrich von Gärtner.
quote: King Otto I commissioned the Bavarian architect Friedrich von Gärtner

not-open.label: supported
not-open.says: The Parliament is not open to the public; the National Gardens beside it are.
quote: surrounded by the extensive National Gardens, which are open to the public; the Parliament itself is not open to the public

tomb.label: supported
tomb.says: The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is a cenotaph for Greek soldiers killed in war, unveiled on 25 March 1932.
quote: It is a cenotaph dedicated to the Greek soldiers killed during war.
The Tomb was unveiled on 25 March 1932

sculptor.label: supported
sculptor.says: It was sculpted by Fokion Rok between 1930 and 1932; the figure is a soldier lying on the ground.
quote: It was sculpted between 1930 and 1932 by sculptor Fokion Rok.
a gunner lying on the ground

evzones.label: supported
evzones.says: The guards are Evzones of the Presidential Guard, the last Evzone unit of the Greek army.
quote: The unit is distinguished as the last unit of Evzones in the Hellenic Army

still.label: supported
still.says: Guards move slowly and stylised, switch positions every fifteen minutes and stand motionless between.
quote: Guards on duty perform their movements in a very slow and highly stylized manner.
They switch positions with each other every fifteen minutes and remain completely motionless and at attention in the meantime.

hourly.label: supported
hourly.says: A change takes place every hour on the hour.
quote: The "little changes" take place every hour on the hour
Catch the changing of the guards in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in front of Parliament every hour on the hour.

kilt.label: supported
kilt.says: The fustanella kilt uses 30 metres of white cloth.
quote: a cotton kilt made from 30 meters (98 feet) of white cloth

pleats.label: tradition
pleats.says: The kilt is said to have 400 pleats for the 400 years of Ottoman rule.
quote: with supposedly 400 pleats (πιέτες) representing the 400 years of Ottoman occupation

shoes.label: supported
shoes.says: The red clogs with black pompoms weigh about 1.5 kilos each.
quote: red leather clogs with black pompons
On average each tsarouchi weighs approximately 1.5 kilos

klephts.label: supported
klephts.says: The uniform comes from the clothes of the klephts, fighters of the War of Independence.
quote: which evolved from the clothes worn by the klephts in the Greek War of Independence

everyday.label: supported
everyday.says: The everyday uniform is a long tunic, navy blue in winter and light khaki in summer.
quote: a long tunic which is the everyday uniform
The basic color of the winter doulamas is navy blue
while the summer version is light khaki

formal.label: supported
formal.says: Formal dress with the fustanella is worn on Sundays, national holidays and special occasions.
quote: Formal dress, which is worn on Sundays, on important national holidays, at the reception of foreign dignitaries and on other special occasions, consists of the farion, ypoditis, foustanela

grand.label: supported
grand.says: The Grand Change is at 11 am on Sunday mornings with the whole guard and a military band.
quote: The Grand Change takes place at 11 am on Sunday mornings, and involves the whole Guard with its officers and a military band

sunday.label: supported
sunday.says: On certain days there is a ceremonial change with a band and most of the 120 Evzones at 11 am.
quote: On certain days, a ceremonial changing of the guard occurs with an army band and the majority of the 120 Evzones present at 11 am.

parts.name: The square
parts.stand: At the top of the marble steps on the east side of the square, facing the big pale building across the avenue.

paras.t: This is Syntagma, which means Constitution. The square is named for the constitution the first king of Greece, Otto, was forced to grant after an uprising on 3 September 1843.

The building across the road was Otto's palace, designed by the Bavarian architect Friedrich von Gärtner, and begun in 1836. In 1929 the government decided it would house Parliament for good, and the Senate first met there in 1934. The Parliament isn't open to visitors, but the National Gardens beside it are.

parts.name: The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
parts.stand: Cross at the lights and stand at the edge of the open space in front of the Parliament, facing the carved wall with the guards. Stay behind any barrier.

paras.t: The carved wall is the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, a memorial for every Greek soldier killed in war. The sculptor Fokion Rok carved a fallen soldier lying on the ground, and it was unveiled on 25 March 1932.

The guards are Evzones, from the Presidential Guard, the last Evzone unit in the Greek army. Watch them. They hold perfectly still, and every fifteen minutes they swap places in slow, highly stylised moves. A changeover happens every hour on the hour.

The uniform comes from the fighters of the War of Independence. On most days the guards wear a long tunic, navy blue in winter and light khaki in summer. On Sundays and holidays they wear the white kilt, the fustanella, made from 30 metres of cloth. Tradition says it has 400 pleats, one for each year of Ottoman rule. And those red clogs with the black pompoms weigh around 1.5 kilos each.
On Sunday mornings at 11 there's the Grand Change, with the whole guard, its officers and a military band.
Please don't touch the guards or step into their path. They are on duty at a war memorial.

practical.t: The change of the guard usually happens every hour on the hour, and the Grand Change on Sundays at 11 am. Check before you plan around it, since ceremonies can change.
